STEP 1 - Scene: This looks like a plate of cooked meat, probably beef or pork ribs/short rib pieces with some charred edges and a few crumbs. It is photographed from above (near top-down), with the plate on a glass-topped table.

STEP 2 - Ruler: A square white plate, roughly 26 cm across its outer edge. Area ≈ 26 x 26 x ~0.85 (rounded corners) ≈ 575 cm²; using a round-equivalent of 26 cm diameter gives 530 cm². I'll use ~550 cm².

STEP 3 - Items: (1) Cooked meat pieces with fat and bone-like strips, (2) a few small crumbs/bits of meat on the table and plate, (3) some brown juice/fat smears on the plate.

STEP 4 - Area: Meat pile covers about 12% of the plate (~66 cm²). Small crumbs and smears are negligible (<1%). Total food coverage ≈ 13%.

STEP 5 - Volume: Meat pile ~66 cm² x ~1.5 cm height (irregular, layered pieces) ≈ 100 ml. The stray crumb on the table is excluded as it is off the plate, though it adds a few grams.

STEP 6 - Grams: 100 ml x 0.9 (meat density, includes some bone/fat gaps) ≈ 90 g. Adding small crumbs and juice residue ≈ 95 g total.

STEP 7 - Energy: Cooked meat with fat, roughly 250 kcal/100 g (fatty cooked beef/pork ribs). 95 g x 2.5 = ~240 kcal.

STEP 8 - Sanity check: A modest pile of cooked meat remnants on a large plate, around 95 g and ~240 kcal, is plausible. It is not a full serving, which fits the sparse coverage.
